core_relation.sentence: The reliability of the gospel proclamation depends on the early creeds being genuinely pre-Pauline and datable to the 30s AD, which in turn depends on the creeds not being expanded into myth over time.
core_relation.quote: What keeps the creeds from being expanded until they become myth and they're not really the words of the eyewitnesses. [S063]

core_relation_run2.sentence: The reliability of the earliest Christian proclamation depends on the creeds being pre-Pauline and therefore datable to within a few years of the crucifixion, which is established by the convergence of early creedal material, Paul's conversion timeline, and critical scholars' own admissions.
core_relation_run2.quote: So that presumes a previous material before first Cor- first Thess. [S024]

product_test.quote: What keeps the creeds from being expanded until they become myth and they're not really the words of the eyewitnesses. [S063]
product_test.reason: If the creedal material is not early (i.e., the temporal gap is zero or the creeds postdate the eyewitnesses), the argument for their reliability collapses entirely rather than merely weakening. The whole case rests on the conjunction of early dating AND pre-Pauline origin AND non-expansion; remove any one and the conclusion fails, not just diminishes.

slots.plays_role: External negentropy influx — the outside source that sustains the argument is the consensus of critical scholars (even hostile ones like the Jesus Seminar and Bart Ehrman) who independently grant the early dating; this external testimony keeps the coherence from collapsing into mere apologetic assertion.
slots.quote: And yet they say, always remember this, the Jesus Seminar took a vote, and they say in volume two, toward the back, they say that the 1 Corinthians 15:3 and following, three to five or more verses, um Paul's, it's not Paul, but Paul cites a creed. [S045]

slots.plays_role: Alignment — the coupling between the creed and its reference (the historical Jesus and the eyewitnesses) is strongest when the creed is aligned with what the eyewitnesses actually taught before Paul's conversion.
slots.quote: They said that creed or its component parts was already in existence before Paul took his walk to Damascus. [S047]

slots.plays_role: Signal fidelity — whether the truth of the eyewitness testimony survives transmission through the oral tradition and into the written creeds without corruption into myth.
slots.quote: What keeps the creeds from being expanded until they become myth and they're not really the words of the eyewitnesses. [S063]

slots.plays_role: Effective entropy — the expansion of the creeds into myth over time is the entropic degradation that lowers coherence; the shorter the gap, the less entropy accumulates.
slots.quote: What keeps the creeds from being expanded until they become myth and they're not really the words of the eyewitnesses. [S063]

slots.plays_role: Temporal integration — the time between the cross (30 AD) and the writing of the earliest books (1 Thessalonians, ~48-50 AD) is the accumulated consequence that makes the creeds early and therefore reliable.
slots.quote: Put this way 33 to 48 is only 15 years. [S013]

slots.plays_role: Compression — the creeds themselves are compressed, ordered summaries of the gospel (deity, death, resurrection) that compress meaning and resist noise.
slots.quote: That's the classic gospel of deity, death, resurrection. [S054]

slots.plays_role: Phase transition — the conversion of Paul (two to three years after the cross) is a threshold event that changes state, marking the point before which the creed must already have existed.
slots.quote: If he became a Christian two to three years after the cross, that means that at probably plus two, cuz it happened before Paul's two to three. [S049]

slots.plays_role: Superposition — the open possibility of the creed's dating remains unresolved (30s, 40s, 50s) until actualized by the scholarly consensus and the textual evidence.
slots.quote: But I think to say the 30s before 40, very common. [S060]

slots.plays_role: Non-local correlation — the creeds in Romans, 1 Corinthians, and 1 Thessalonians are correlated across different letters and locations, showing they are not independent but share a common early source.
slots.quote: Rome Romans has some of the major ones. Romans 10:9, Romans 1:3 and 4. Um first Corinthians is not even that late and first Corinthians 15:3 and following. [S031-S033]

slots.plays_role: Integration — the local integrator is the community of eyewitnesses and the early church that preserved and transmitted the creed before Paul wrote it down.
slots.quote: Because he never gives definitions. And to a Greek culture it'd be really iffy to say Lord in Greek and assume they have the same view of Lord as you do. [S020-S021]

one_line: The paper's argument for early creedal reliability maps onto the master equation as a multiplicative chain where early dating, pre-Pauline origin, and non-expansion must all hold, with time and signal fidelity as the most direct slots.
breaks: The paper treats the scholarly consensus as a supporting factor, but the argument can proceed even if some scholars dissent; the product test is somewhat softened by the rhetorical use of hostile witnesses (Jesus Seminar, Ehrman) as corroboration rather than necessary conditions.
The slot Q (superposition) is stretched — the dating question is not truly held in unresolved possibility; the paper argues it is already resolved by the evidence.
The paper adds an extra factor not in the master equation: the authority of Paul as an eyewitness and the seven undisputed books, which functions as a separate warrant beyond the creedal dating.
The paper is a spoken interview, not a formal argument, so the 'product test' is inferred from the logic of the dating argument rather than stated as a formal equation.

Slot Q (superposition) is weakly present—the paper does not explicitly treat the dating as an unresolved possibility that is later actualized; it presents the dating as already settled by the evidence.
Slot M (alignment) is stretched: the paper does not develop a theory of alignment; it simply notes Paul's anger as consistent with the creed's content.

The paper adds an extra factor not in the master equation: the authority of critical scholars' admissions (the Jesus Seminar, Bart Ehrman, Bultmann). This functions as a social-epistemic warrant rather than a physical factor.
extra_factors: The seven undisputed Pauline books (Romans, 1-2 Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, 1 Thessalonians, Philemon) as a special class of evidence that critics grant.
The argument from Paul's pre-conversion knowledge and anger as evidence the creed predates him.
The admissions of critical scholars (Jesus Seminar, Bart Ehrman, Bultmann) function as an independent warrant for the early dating, not captured by any slot in the master equation.
The 'seven books' of Paul (Romans, 1-2 Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, 1 Thessalonians, Philemon) serve as a fixed corpus that critics grant, providing a stable anchor for the argument.
